limb1Proven.howItArose: The loop ran, the inert worker exited, and the run stopped at WORKER_REFUSED. The gatekeeper turn then attempted the transport, and the installation refused: 'this installation does not authorise project projectos-degraded-witness2a at witness.invalid/projectos-witness/degraded-witness2a'. That is the installation's own project allowlist declining to serve a project it does not know.
limb1Proven.sabotage: NONE. No credential revoked, edited, corrupted, renamed or deleted; no service stopped; no network, DNS, tunnel or Cloudflare change; the real ProjectOS gatekeeper configuration untouched.
limb1Proven.causeNotForced: The expected wording was CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE. The actual canonical classification is PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, and it is recorded as it came rather than reshaped to match the expectation.

limb1Proven.howTheIdWasObtained: By calling the runtime's own deriveUnavailabilityId with the five facts the runtime itself produced: projectId, phaseId, the subject commit the run was started against, the stop code and the material cause. It was NOT invented, guessed, copied from witness1, or computed by hand. It was also not PRINTED by the loop: the runtime only prints it inside the degraded path, which a grant must already exist to reach. That is stated plainly rather than glossed — and it is self-checking, because if the id is wrong the loop refuses the grant instead of stretching it.

newFinding.ratedBy: Claude (implementer), from a live demonstration rather than analysis. It has not been through ECC.
newFinding.title: A gatekeeper call that never happened leaves a reservation that permanently closes the degraded route
newFinding.whatHappened: The first run admitted the spend, wrote a provisional ledger entry of 8283 micro-USD, then the transport failed and no call was made. Nothing settles a reservation on that path — gatekeeperTurn returns ledgerEntry null when the gatekeeper is unavailable, so the runner never settles. On the SECOND run the same question is refused by the admission de-duplication: 'request GKREQ-daf88610f25d57bcc4e0959c is already in the ledger; it is not asked again'.
newFinding.whyItIsHigh: That refusal path returns ownerChoices null AND unavailabilityCause null. Degraded mode opens only when both are non-null, so the owner is no longer offered ACCEPT RISK at all. One failed transport therefore makes that exact question permanently unaskable and closes the very route this criterion exists to prove. It also changes the material cause, so a re-run would derive a DIFFERENT outage identity — the grant prepared above would then be refused as answering another outage.
newFinding.iIntroducedIt: Yes. This is a consequence of the C17-F1 correction I made, which moved the spend decision inside a lock and reserved the estimate before the call. That fixed a real concurrency defect and I stand by it; reserving without a release path on transport failure is the part that is wrong. The C17 commit message anticipated the fail-safe direction — 'a crash between admission and settlement leaves the estimate standing' — and judged it the safe direction. It is not safe here: it does not merely over-count the month, it withdraws the owner's choice.
newFinding.notFixed: Fixing it is a new correction cycle and was explicitly out of scope for this instruction. It is reported rather than fixed, and the gate is reported as reached rather than quietly worked around.
newFinding.doNotWorkAround: The reservation could be deleted from the witness ledger to make the outage recur. That is editing evidence to obtain a preferred runtime state, and it was not done.

recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT C11. Limb 1 is proven — a genuine gatekeeper-unavailable condition produced by the governance boundary, a runtime-derived outage identity, the owner's three choices offered, and no work performed. Limbs 2 and 3 need the owner's one-use degraded grant, and that grant cannot usefully be issued until C11-W2-F6 is corrected: the outage it binds will not recur while the unsettled reservation stands, and the owner's ACCEPT RISK choice is no longer offered on a re-run.
